root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: RustCathedral turns the owner's maze, guarded machines and salvage paradise with a temper into a place the colony learns to work within. Intentional metal passages make the walls both the route and the treasure: ordinary plate is free salvage, richer remains tempt you farther, and sacred structures and deep extraction carry consequences. The hum and the small bolts' changing movements let you notice those consequences without explaining the place's secrets; coolant eels and land-cleaning machines make its sparse life feel maintained, and the rare machinery cycle makes the whole plateau pause. A peaceful, worn-out borehulk offers a longer commitment: remove and transport its heavy drill head for refurbishment, bring back unusual parts, then restore it and choose between an expensive mining servant and a free machine that answers favours elsewhere. Bolts that ride the ship stay lively companions, show unsettling reactions to what the colony does, and eventually present their already-ruled dilemma. Each promise needs a demonstration in ordinary colony play. The free biome owns these mechanics; the campaign owns its hidden relationship and revelations, while shared systems own sun, water confinement and generic creature behaviour.

asks.title: ASK FIRST — What makes this the Rust Cathedral?
asks.picture: The colony enters deliberate metal passages, mines ordinary plate, then hesitates beside an untouched patterned wall while the hum changes. Later it meets the worn borehulk and carries a few dancing bolts away on its ship.
asks.text: Which part of that day makes this your salvage paradise with a temper, and where does the proposed root promise the wrong experience?
asks.why: F1/F2. The owner's sentence is settled; my expansion must give the right weight to the maze, its guards and its responses, without making the repair or ship features disappear.
asks.guess: The ordinary salvage expedition is the centre. The giant and the ship bolts extend the relationship beyond that first visit.
asks.tree_change: If the expedition leads, organise the root around entering, taking, noticing and choosing. If the relationship leads, put repeated visits first while retaining maze, guard and salvage obligations. A correction changes the dependent claims; no answer approves nothing.
asks.decision: What makes this the Rust Cathedral?

asks.title: ASK FIRST — The first demonstration
asks.picture: Three scene drafts: A, a small working salvage camp inside the maze, with a safe extraction beside a sacred boundary and a readable response; B, the long repair trip and the first useful day with the restored borehulk; C, bolts aboard the ship, a witnessed sale, their strange reaction and the return to the plateau.
asks.text: Which scene should come first when you judge whether we understood the mod, and what one failure there would make you stop the demonstration?
asks.why: F1–F3. I found no recorded owner flagship pick. A list of loaded definitions cannot choose the mod's face.
asks.guess: A first. The everyday maze and its manners should earn belief before the longer repair and ship stories.
asks.tree_change: The chosen scene becomes showcase 1 only after a real owner pick. The other built features still need coverage. Later showcases must add different play; each feature keeps its own acceptance scene and shared interactions keep theirs.

asks.title: A maze that changes the route
asks.picture: A salvage crew can see rich metal across a wall. One route follows a long repeating passage; another would open a shortcut through ordinary plate. Farther along is ground held by machines. The current wall scatter supplies random groups; it does not establish this deliberate layout.
asks.text: What should make you choose to follow the passage instead of mining straight through it?
asks.why: F1. 'Intentional maze' must change a real expedition, not merely resemble a circuit board when zoomed out. Guardian purpose is already defence, never a hunting force.
asks.guess: Useful routes and recognisable protected places: opening a shortcut saves work today but can put the crew into a guarded space. Ordinary bulk salvage remains freely mineable.
asks.tree_change: If navigation is the point, add a route-choice scene with an attractive reachable destination and a real shortcut control. If guarded work areas give the maze meaning, add boundary and guard-response checks. If the pattern mainly communicates the builders' intention, bind that visual judgment after a labelled mock and walk; do not invent tactical rules.
asks.decision: A maze that changes the route

asks.title: A warning in a busy colony
asks.picture: Forty colonists are busy on the plateau. Several fishing and salvage jobs overlap. The hum changes, bolts nearby alter their figures, and work on the borehulk can be refused. No screen explains the hidden machinery. Today the default stage ceiling can leave the hum sounding calm despite anger; that is a contradiction to resolve, not the proposed experience.
asks.text: What should reach your attention soon enough to make you pause the right work, and what should you still have to work out for yourself?
asks.why: F2. A response can exist in saved state and still give the player no usable chance to react. The established secrecy rules forbid solving this with an explanation of the mind.
asks.guess: A noticeable sound change and nearby bolt behaviour, with a plain refusal on the specific order; enough time to stop the offending work, without an explanation of the cause behind the place.
asks.tree_change: If sound and movement are sufficient, require an ordinary busy-colony observation and response window, with a quiet-work control. If a one-time interruption is essential, add that bounded cue and its repetition limit. If a reader must identify which activity matters, specify that narrow information and prove it without revealing forbidden lore.
asks.decision: A warning in a busy colony

asks.title: The next visit after an offence
asks.picture: Yesterday a crew took a few eels and left when the tones worsened. Another crew damaged a sacred structure. Today each returns to do only ordinary plate salvage. Temporary irritation decays in code; accumulated standing has no general recovery route I found. The campaign's deliberate betrayal is a separate, already-ruled permanent loss.
asks.text: What should each crew have to do before working comfortably here again?
asks.why: F2. Existing intent makes desecration survivable and repentance expensive; it does not supply a complete free-biome recovery action. Waiting away every offence or permanent low-grade punishment can each miss that intent.
asks.guess: Minor disturbance eases with time and careful work; sacred damage needs a meaningful act of repayment. I would keep the costs and signs different, without proposing a new ritual.
asks.tree_change: If time is enough for minor irritation, bind a return-after-rest scene and a continuing-offence control. If ordinary respectful work repairs standing, define that bounded credit and prevent idle farming. If sacred damage requires restitution, specify the concrete payment/action and its readable result. If he says it does not matter, add no recovery leaf beyond settled economics; never turn this into a waiver without his words.
asks.decision: The next visit after an offence

asks.title: The owned borehulk earns its cost
asks.picture: The colony has transported the head, paid for refurbishment and spent the unusual parts. On its first working day you mark a real surface excavation while the rest of the colony has jobs to do. It will need service and the political cost remains. Directed surface mining is already promised; deep drilling is outside this payoff.
asks.text: What job should that first day finish that would make you say the repair was worth the trouble?
asks.why: F3. A ten-times-speed setting can pass arithmetic while yielding an awkward machine that needs constant attention or cannot reach useful work.
asks.guess: A substantial excavation that frees several colonists for other work, with one area order and a clear service warning. Its power should be obvious through work completed.
asks.tree_change: A whole room/quarry task gives a completion and material-yield acceptance scene. A continuous industrial role needs a longer run with hauling and a service cycle. If the delight is watching the machine work, add a separate movement/sound judgment as well as completed work. The answer sets the payoff bar, not permission to weaken mining wherever surface cells are reachable.
asks.decision: The owned borehulk earns its cost

asks.title: A free machine doing you a favour
asks.picture: You freed the restored borehulk. Later, away from the Cathedral, you ask for help with a large marked excavation. It arrives as a friend, works for a while and returns home. There are more marked cells than it can finish during the provisional stay. It still takes no direct orders and never mines the Cathedral for you.
asks.text: What should you be able to count on getting done before it leaves?
asks.why: F3. The free branch's favour is already settled. Its practical commitment is not settled by a provisional visit timer or an instantly appearing helper.
asks.guess: A clearly useful share of the work, with a readable departure time and no disappearance in the middle of an unclear promise. It can leave unfinished work when that was clear from the start.
asks.tree_change: A timed contribution needs useful output and honest arrival/departure cues, including inaccessible work. A promised finite job needs a defined accepted job boundary and an ending condition. A task chosen by the machine needs its selection made legible. Every answer retains favours, no orders, cooldown and the Cathedral exclusion.
asks.decision: A free machine doing you a favour

asks.title: The hull pets have been paying attention
asks.picture: Far from the plateau, the colony sells some dead smartsteel. The hull bolts briefly stop and turn. Days later a cold mark is visible under them. A reader notices enough for the existing dilemma, and a later Cathedral landing begins uneasily. Keeping them or prying them off is already the ruled choice.
asks.text: What connection should a careful player be able to make before that choice, so the uneasy return feels earned?
asks.why: F2/F3. The built ledger can collect an act while nobody sees its short tell, including during travel. The mystery should be preserved without a consequence that feels unrelated to anything the player saw.
asks.guess: The player can connect a few specific transactions to repeated bolt reactions, then recognise the same altered behaviour on return. The campaign reveal supplies the identity of the listener at its proper gate.
asks.tree_change: If repeated observed acts are enough, require that sequence with an unrelated-sale/no-bolt control. If a missed tell must leave a trace, add only that observational trace, not an explanation of the secret. If understanding may wait until the reveal, require the reveal to connect the already-seen events fairly. The spying, permanent pets and remove/leave fork are not reopened.
asks.decision: The hull pets have been paying attention
